newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares surge five percent on govt hopes.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares surge five percent on govt hopes.

text.p: The prospect of Turkey's main opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz forming an "Islamist-free" coalition sent shares soaring over five percent on Monday.

Analysts said the market put aside doubts about Yilmaz's ability to muster necessary parliamentary support for a secularist government in a surge of optimism triggered his appointment as prime minister-designate late on Friday.

The IMKB National-100 index leapt 5.3 percent, or 87 points, to end the morning session at 1,729, in sight of an all-time, intraday high of 1,751. Trading volume surged to an unusually high 21.59 trillion ($147 million), more than double Friday's 10.26 trillion.

"The market is overreacting but it has good reasons," said Atilla Yesilada, head of reasearch at Global Securities. "It seems they are taking a heavy bet on Yilmaz forming a government and the bond market is doing the same," he said.

Bond yields fell to around 100 percent from 104.5 percent at the end of last week. Bankers said market participants were ignoring the lack of progress on macro-economic policies in favour of short-term, speculative trading.
"This is technical buying guided by short-term developments, while no medium- or long-term steps have been taken on the economic front," said one official from a private bank.
The Turkish lira eased to 146,480 against the dollar from a close of 145,870 on Friday in line with a firmer dollar/mark parity.

Yilmaz called a meeting of his conservative Motherland Party on Monday to plan strategy for his bid to forge a coalition of parties from the left and right to keep out the Islamists of outgoing prime minister Necmettin Erbakan.
To be successful such a bid would need the support of around a dozen MPs from the rival conservative True Path Party, which under Tansu Ciller is allied with Erbakan's Welfare Party.
Uncertainty over the level of backing for Yilmaz was expected to limit the short-term upside potential, brokers said.
"The market will not sustain these levels unless Yilmaz gains the vote of confidence," Yesilada said, adding that it was almost impossible to predict which way the vote would go.
"Whatever happens we are in for a turbulent time going into elections," he said. Yilmaz has said any government formed by him would seek elections next spring.
The ground swell of positive sentiment was reinforced by the weekend resignation of a dissident MP from Ciller's faction in the wake of President Suleyman Demirel's decision to nominate Yilmaz.

Islamist Erbakan stepped down last week after months of open criticism from the secularist army, which had fuelled political uncertainty and undermined significant share gains at the start of the year.
Technical analysts said the historical intraday high of 1,751 was within reach, but some brokers said such a move was unlikely until the formation of a government.
"I do not expect a break through the historical peak before the government is formed," said Fatma Kaya of Ekinciler Securities.
Share trading activity was led by utility Cukurova Elektrik, state oil refiner Tupras and flat steel maker Eregli.
"In particular, the movements in Eregli lifted the market as a whole upwards," said Mustafa Toprak of Es Securities. "I expect the gains to continue until the close."
Eregli has a strong impact on the market index because of its high market capitalisation.
($1 = 146,480 Turkish lira)
